probe: Siril seqpsf on an ALIGNED arm pair — the tool-search claim, executed
why: seqpsf is a REGISTERED refusal for the absolute measurement: it converts a position ONCE and measures that same pixel area in every image, which cannot follow a star across a drifting sequence (m = -2.104 in the reference block against +3.55/+5.05/+3.63 in the others). That disqualifying behaviour is CORRECT for a differential pair, where the arms are pixel-aligned and the star does not move — so the claim had to be re-probed here rather than inherited.
how: arm_A.fit and arm_B.fit symlinked as a 2-image sequence pr_, setphot -inner=20 -outer=30 -aperture=10 -dyn_ratio=0.5, seqpsf pr 1 -at=2204,2808

agreement_mag.note: the psf log prints 4 decimals, so this IS the rounding

verdict: seqpsf WORKS here and returns the same magnitudes as the adopted per-image psf path to 1e-5 mag. Not adopted because it measures one star per invocation from a selection — the same per-star, per-image call as psf — with a parser that is not the one already validated in this repo. Recorded as a POSITIVE cross-validation of the photometry, not as a gap.
